title: What to know before you try peptides
excerpt: They’re sold as shortcuts to muscle, healing, weight loss, even a sharper brain. Here’s the honest map of what works, what doesn’t, and where the real risks are.

title: Can a brain implant read the voice in your head?
excerpt: A brain implant caught sentences a person only imagined. The same study shows how limited, and how careful, that reading has to be.

title: How can one drug treat both depression and anxiety?
excerpt: The same SSRI is a first choice for depression and for panic, social anxiety, and OCD. That one fact strains the chemical imbalance story.

title: What happens when you put prism glasses on a barn owl?
excerpt: Fit a young owl with prisms that shift its world sideways and the map of sound in its brain quietly slides over to match.

title: Do the new Alzheimer's drugs actually work?
excerpt: A 2023 trial cleared amyloid plaque from people's brains with the drug donanemab and modestly slowed their decline. What that bought, and what it cost.

title: Scientists found an aggression switch in the mouse brain.
excerpt: In a 2011 study, switching on a pinhead of neurons in the mouse hypothalamus made a calm male attack almost anything in front of it.

title: You use all of your brain.
excerpt: The idea that ninety percent of your brain sits idle, waiting to be unlocked, is one of the most popular myths about the mind. It is wrong.

title: Dopamine doesn't do what you think it does.
excerpt: Dopamine is not the brain's pleasure chemical. It signals reward prediction error, the gap between what you expected and what actually happened.

title: What is a neuron, really?
excerpt: A neuron is not just a brain cell that sends signals. Build the real one from scratch and the rest of the brain starts to make sense.

title: How does memory actually work?
excerpt: A memory is not a recording filed away in a drawer. It is a physical change in your neurons, rebuilt every time you remember.

title: Why do you need to sleep?
excerpt: You spend a third of your life unconscious and you cannot skip it. For something that costly, sleep must be doing real work.

title: Why can't most drugs reach your brain?
excerpt: You can swallow a pill and it reaches your whole body, yet most drugs never reach your brain. The blood-brain barrier is why.

title: What does an fMRI actually measure?
excerpt: When a headline says a brain region lit up, what was measured? Not thoughts, and not even electricity. Blood, measured indirectly, and a few seconds late.

title: Brain myths that won't die
excerpt: Eight ideas about the brain that feel true, get repeated everywhere, and fall apart the moment you check them against the research.

title: The Lab
excerpt: Small experiments you run on your own brain, right in the page. Quick, honest demonstrations of how the mind actually works.

title: Find your blind spot
excerpt: A quick blind spot test you run in the page. Cover one eye, stare at the cross, and watch the dot vanish where the optic nerve leaves the retina.

title: The Stroop test
excerpt: Take the Stroop test in your browser. Name the ink color while your brain wants to read the word, then measure the Stroop effect in your own milliseconds.

title: Reaction time test
excerpt: A simple visual reaction time test you run on yourself. Wait for green, react as fast as you can, and see your median time next to typical values.
